label: sparse, weakly h/r-associated (copy-phase h input before outputting r; late original steps of h/r-initial sequences)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps) with weak magnitude (median 0.12). Activation is enriched for the letters h and r: copy-phase steps whose input is h (about 46% of mass, often when the output is r, i.e. the original had h followed by r), and the last one or two original-phase steps or the delimiter in sequences that start with h or r. It never fires at t<3, and almost never in sequences where the copy went wrong. Each of these contexts gives precision of only about 1-10%: most copy-phase h->r steps do not activate it, and nothing simple separates the ones that do. The best single predicate (copy-phase input h, output r) gets F1 about 0.15. A disjunction with the h/r-initial late-original clause reaches 66% recall but only 1% precision. I found no coherent predicate.
